summary: Balance surface detail and an explicitly approximate subsurface response without turning a character into uniform wax.
objective: Give a character skin-like light response while preserving facial form and an explicit approximation boundary.
intent_signals: Give a character skin-like light response while preserving facial form and an explicit approximation boundary.
example_prompts: Light a stylized character with readable cheek planes and restrained scattering at thin ear edges, without claiming measured human tissue.

principles: Keep facial geometry, surface reflection and subsurface response as separate decisions. An extra warm edge tint can be an authored cue but is not automatically a physical scattering model.
Use measured tissue parameters only when their subject, units and model assumptions are actually available; character palette does not determine biological properties.
implementation: Establish silhouette and facial planes before microdetail. Scale pores and wrinkle relief to the intended shot; use mesh detail for deep creases that need real occlusion rather than pushing all texture through a strong normal map.

For a subsurface-capable renderer, choose a documented transport approximation and track its length scale relative to the object. For a simpler style, label a warm-rim or diffuse-wrap treatment as an appearance approximation.

Compare front, side and back lighting under fixed exposure. Tune surface roughness separately from scattering so a broad highlight does not erase the nose or lips and subsurface softness does not flood every shadow equally.
observable_checks: Front-lit facial planes remain readable when subsurface response is enabled; the result is not uniformly luminous.
A thin feature and a thicker cheek respond differently in the chosen setup, or the simplified model's inability to distinguish them is recorded.
Rescaling the character prompts a check of scattering length and pore scale; parameters are not assumed invariant in every renderer.

known_limits: No medical, physiological, demographic or measured tissue claim; optical parameters do not establish softness, elasticity or contact friction.
Authored modeling and inspection guidance; no runtime artifact or improvement has been observed for this record.
creative_affordances: Deeply stylized palettes, painted skin and deliberately wax-like characters remain possible when intended; photorealistic skin is not mandatory.

claims.statement: Jensen and colleagues' 2001 subsurface model combines single scattering with a diffusion approximation for multiple scattering, and includes skin among the materials used in optical-property measurements.
claims.scope: Description of the cited model and its reported examples; no universal skin coefficients or calibration for this profile.
